name: Milk (cow)
description: The daily glass, chai base, and kheer canvas.

tcm.note: Neutral-moistening; TCM uses it for dryness.

ayurveda.note: The classic cooling, building food — warm milk is still shita-virya.

unani.note: Doodh is thanda-tar; hence warming additions like haldi or saffron.

histamine.note: Fresh pasteurized milk is low; the aged/fermented dairy family is where trouble starts.

nutrition.highlight: calcium in the form the body handles best

name: Yogurt
description: Cultured milk — and the traditions' most famous disagreement.

tcm.note: Thinly classified; modern TCM leans cool-damp.

ayurveda.note: The classic surprise: dahi is USHNA (sour, channel-clogging) — avoid at night.

unani.note: Dahi is textbook thanda in desi/Unani usage — the exact opposite of Ayurveda.

histamine.note: Fermented but young; fine for many, borderline for the very sensitive.

nutrition.highlight: live cultures, and the traditions' loudest disagreement

name: Buttermilk (chaas)
description: Thin churned yogurt drink, salted and spiced.

tcm.note: Not classical.

ayurveda.note: Takra is milder than dahi — praised as digestive; schools call it mildly heating yet pitta-manageable.

unani.note: Chaas/ayran is the everyday summer cooler.

histamine.note: As yogurt.

name: Paneer
description: Fresh unaged pressed cheese of palak paneer.

tcm.note: Not classical.

ayurveda.note: Fresh cheese = heavy, building, cooling-leaning.

histamine.note: Fresh unaged cheese — far safer than aged.

nutrition.highlight: protein-dense, and it will not melt

name: Ghee
description: Clarified butter — sacred fat of two traditions.

tcm.note: Fats read warming in TCM.

ayurveda.note: The famous answer: ghee is SHITA-virya — cooling, pitta's best fat.

unani.note: Desi folk calls ghee garam — another clean tradition split.

histamine.note: Milk solids removed — the safest dairy fat.

nutrition.highlight: pure butterfat — the milk solids are gone

name: Butter
description: Everyday dairy fat.

tcm.note: Thin classical documentation.

ayurveda.note: Fresh makkhan is cooling-building.

unani.note: Some hakims group it with ghee (garam), others call fresh makkhan cool.

histamine.note: Well tolerated; minimal protein.

nutrition.highlight: vitamin A rides in the fat

name: Cream
description: Rich milk fat of qorma and qishta desserts.

ayurveda.note: Heavy-building like milk.

histamine.note: Fresh cream low; whipped/aged products vary.

nutrition.highlight: fat enough to whip, which milk cannot

name: Fresh cheese (mozzarella/akkawi)
description: Young white cheeses — pizza's stretch and kunafa's heart.

tcm.note: Not classical.

ayurveda.note: As fresh cheese.

histamine.note: SIGHI rates fresh mozzarella 0 — unripened cheese is not an aged one.

name: Aged cheese
description: Matured hard cheeses — flavor built by the very aging that builds histamine.

tcm.note: Not classical; rich-aged foods lean warm.

ayurveda.note: Aged + sour = heating, tamasic.

unani.note: Aged jibn leans garam in Unani sources.

histamine.note: The textbook high-histamine food — months of aging = maximal amines.

nutrition.highlight: calcium-dense, and the flavour is the ageing

name: Labneh
description: Thick strained yogurt eaten with zaatar and oil.

tcm.note: Not classical.

ayurveda.note: Follows dahi (sour, concentrated).

unani.note: Follows laban's cooling nature in Arab usage.

histamine.note: As yogurt, slightly concentrated.

nutrition.highlight: yogurt with the water strained out

name: Ice cream
description: Frozen sweet cream — physically cold, energetically argued over.

tcm.note: TCM warns cold-damp foods 'injure the spleen' — cooling but not recommended for it.

ayurveda.note: Cooling but heavy and ama-forming.

histamine.note: Base is modest; chocolate/strawberry flavors inherit those triggers.

name: Greek yogurt
description: Yogurt with the whey strained out — thicker, and double the protein.

tcm.note: Follows plain yogurt; straining removes water, not nature.

ayurveda.note: Dahi is ushna whatever you strain out of it.

unani.note: Thanda like dahi, though less watery than the desi original.

histamine.note: Young culture, like plain yogurt — the aged cheeses are the problem, not this.

nutrition.highlight: double the protein of plain yogurt

name: Feta
description: Salty brined white cheese, crumbled over everything from salad to eggs.

tcm.note: Brined cheese is not a classical TCM entry; placed by analogy to fresh dairy.

ayurveda.note: Sour plus salty plus fermented reads ushna, unlike fresh paneer.

unani.note: Salt and ripening push it toward garam; the classical texts describe fresh cheese, not this.

histamine.note: SIGHI rates it 1 — brine-ripened, so above fresh cheese but below the aged ones.

nutrition.highlight: salty because the brine is what preserves it

name: Halloumi
description: The cheese that grills instead of melting — squeaky, salty, Levantine.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; treated as fresh dairy.

ayurveda.note: Salt-cured and usually cooked over direct heat.

unani.note: Salting dries it; grilling adds to that.

histamine.note: Unripened despite the salt — closer to paneer than to feta on the SIGHI list.

nutrition.highlight: holds its shape on a grill

name: Cottage cheese
description: Loose fresh curds, barely cultured — the plainest cheese there is.

tcm.note: Fresh dairy, neutral and moistening.

ayurveda.note: Fresh unsoured curd stays shita — it is souring that turns dairy ushna.

unani.note: Thanda-tar, the same reading as paneer.

histamine.note: Fresh and lightly cultured; among the safer cheeses for a reactive day.

name: Ricotta
description: Soft, sweet-tasting cheese made from the whey another cheese left behind.

tcm.note: Not classically classified; read as fresh dairy.

ayurveda.note: Fresh and unsoured, so shita like other unfermented curds.

histamine.note: SIGHI rates it 0. Fresh and unripened, though it spoils fast once opened.

name: Cream cheese
description: Spreadable fresh cheese, rich enough to be mostly fat.

tcm.note: Modern product; read as rich fresh dairy, which TCM calls damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Fresh and unsoured, so shita — but very guru, heavy and slow.

unani.note: Cold and wet like the fresh cheeses it belongs with.

histamine.note: SIGHI rates plain cream cheese 0; flavoured tubs inherit whatever is stirred in.

name: Processed cheese
description: Aged cheese melted down with emulsifiers into slices and tubs.

tcm.note: Inherits from the aged cheese it is built out of.

ayurveda.note: An aged base, so ushna, however mild it tastes.

unani.note: Garam by inheritance; no classical entry exists for a processed slice.

histamine.note: Built from ripened cheese, so it carries ripened-cheese histamine — the mild taste hides it.

name: Sour cream
description: Cream soured with cultures — the cooling spoon on a hot plate.

tcm.note: Read with the cultured dairy family.

ayurveda.note: Soured dairy is ushna, the same logic that makes dahi heating.

unani.note: Thanda in practice, which is why it is served against chilli heat.

histamine.note: Cultured but young.

name: Kefir
description: Milk fermented with grains into a thin, fizzy, sharply sour drink.

tcm.note: Not a classical food; placed with cultured milk.

ayurveda.note: Strongly soured, so ushna — more so than plain dahi.

unani.note: Read as a thinner, sourer dahi.

histamine.note: A live, mixed, long ferment — the mechanism that makes kefir interesting is also the one that makes histamine.

name: Condensed milk
description: Milk boiled down with sugar until it pours like syrup.

tcm.note: Long reduction concentrates and warms; sweet and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Cooked down and heavily sweetened — the cooking is what turns milk's shita.

unani.note: Garam by preparation rather than by ingredient.

histamine.note: Heat-treated and sugar-preserved; low in itself.

name: Evaporated milk
description: Milk with most of its water removed, and no sugar added.

tcm.note: Concentrated milk; the nature of milk is not changed by removing water.

ayurveda.note: Still shita, only heavier — unlike its sweetened cousin.

histamine.note: Sterilised in the tin; low.

name: Khoya
description: Milk stirred over heat for hours until only the solids remain — the base of most mithai.

tcm.note: Hours of reduction; TCM reads long-cooked concentrates as warming and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Classically milk keeps its shita virya however far you reduce it — it becomes guru, not ushna.

unani.note: Desi hakimi usage is firm that mawa mithai is garam — the opposite of the classical Ayurvedic reading.

histamine.note: Low in itself; the sweets built on it usually add nuts and khoya sits out at room temperature in shops.

name: Buffalo milk
description: The default milk across much of South Asia — thicker and far richer than cow's.

tcm.note: Not a staple of the Chinese record; read alongside cow's milk.

ayurveda.note: Mahisha dugdha is classically shita and guru, and specifically named as sleep-inducing.

unani.note: Thanda and heavy — more so than cow's milk, which is why it is cut with water for chai.

histamine.note: Fresh milk, low — same as cow's.

nutrition.highlight: nearly twice the fat of cow's milk

name: Goat milk
description: Lighter and easier on the stomach than cow's milk, with a distinct tang.

tcm.note: Goat's milk is explicitly warm in TCM, tonifying — unlike cow's milk, which is neutral.

ayurveda.note: Aja dugdha is shita but light and astringent — classically given in fever, where cow's milk is too heavy.

unani.note: Treated as the most temperate of the milks, close to balanced.

histamine.note: Fresh milk; low.

name: Camel milk
description: Gulf staple — thin, faintly salty, and the one milk the traditions call warming.

tcm.note: Absent from the Chinese record; placed by analogy only.

ayurveda.note: Ushtra dugdha is named ushna — light, slightly salty, and the exception among milks.

unani.note: Garam in Arab and Unani usage, given for chest and digestive complaints.

histamine.note: Fresh milk; low. Often sold raw, which is a separate question from histamine.

name: Blue cheese
description: Cheese deliberately veined with mould and ripened for months.

tcm.note: Read with the aged cheeses; warming and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and very guru — aged, salty and mould-ripened.

histamine.note: Mould-ripened and long-aged — the highest cheese on the SIGHI list, above even hard cheddar.

name: Mascarpone
description: Cream set with acid into a spoonable, barely-cheese richness.

tcm.note: Read with cream and fresh cheese.

ayurveda.note: Shita and extremely guru — almost pure cream.

histamine.note: SIGHI rates it 0 — fresh and unripened, unlike the aged cheeses.

name: Quark
description: Soft fresh curd cheese, thicker than yogurt and milder than cottage cheese.

tcm.note: Fresh dairy; read with the unripened cheeses.

ayurveda.note: Fresh and unsoured, so shita.

histamine.note: Low — fresh and lightly cultured.

name: Milk powder
description: Milk spray-dried to a shelf-stable powder — the base of most packaged sweets and chai.

tcm.note: Read with milk; drying does not change its nature.

ayurveda.note: Shita like milk, though heavier and harder to digest reconstituted.

histamine.note: Heat-processed and stored for months — above fresh milk, and it is in far more products than people expect.

nutrition.highlight: in more things than you think

name: Shrikhand
description: Yogurt hung until thick, then whipped with sugar, saffron and cardamom.

tcm.note: Strained yogurt with warm spices; cooling overall.

ayurveda.note: Dahi is ushna in the classical reading, and the saffron adds to it.

unani.note: Thanda-tar in desi usage — a summer sweet, eaten with puri.

histamine.note: Hung yogurt, held and sweetened — above plain dahi.

name: Mishti doi
description: Bengali yogurt set with caramelised jaggery in an earthen pot.

tcm.note: Yogurt base, sweetened and set.

ayurveda.note: Soured dahi is ushna; the jaggery adds to it.

unani.note: Thanda-tar, though warmer than plain dahi for the gur.

histamine.note: Cultured and then held warm to set — a longer ferment than plain dahi.

name: Clotted cream
description: Cream heated slowly until a thick crust forms and is lifted off.

tcm.note: Read with cream; the slow heating concentrates it.

ayurveda.note: Shita and extremely guru.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; qishta and kaymak are the same idea across two cuisines.

histamine.note: Low; it is fresh cream, only concentrated.

name: Lactose-free milk
description: Ordinary milk with the lactose already split by added enzyme.

tcm.note: Read with milk; the enzyme changes the sugar, not the nature.

ayurveda.note: Shita, as milk is.

histamine.note: Same as milk. Lactose intolerance and histamine intolerance are different problems, often confused.

name: Whey
description: The greenish liquid left when milk curdles — usually poured away.

tcm.note: Read with the cultured dairy family; light and cooling.

ayurveda.note: Shita and laghu — the lightest thing milk becomes.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; drunk rather than thrown away in older practice.

histamine.note: Low fresh; it sours fast.

name: Halloumi-style paneer
description: Firmer pressed paneer made to hold up on skewers and a grill.

tcm.note: Read with paneer, which is neutral and fresh.

ayurveda.note: Shita; grilling warms it in practice.

histamine.note: Low — fresh and unripened, like ordinary paneer.

name: Burrata
description: A mozzarella shell holding shredded curd and cream — meant to be eaten the day it is made.

tcm.note: Fresh cheese and cream.

ayurveda.note: Shita and guru.

histamine.note: Fresh and unripened, so low — but it spoils within days.

nutrition.highlight: eat it the day it's made

name: Provolone
description: Stretched-curd Italian cheese aged from mild to sharp.

tcm.note: Read with the aged cheeses.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Aged cheese.

name: Emmental
description: The holed Swiss cheese, aged for months with a sweet nutty flavour.

tcm.note: Read with the aged cheeses.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Aged cheese — the holes come from the same bacteria that raise histamine.

name: Gruyère
description: Dense alpine cheese aged up to a year — the melting cheese for fondue.

tcm.note: Read with the aged cheeses.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Long-aged.

nutrition.highlight: up to a year in the cave

name: Manchego
description: Firm sheep's-milk cheese from La Mancha, aged from weeks to years.

tcm.note: Read with the aged cheeses.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Aged sheep's milk cheese.

name: Buffalo mozzarella
description: Mozzarella from buffalo milk — softer, tangier and far richer than the cow version.

tcm.note: Fresh cheese; read with mozzarella.

ayurveda.note: Shita, following buffalo milk.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; buffalo milk is the coldest of the milks.

histamine.note: Fresh and unripened, so low.

name: Frozen yogurt
description: Yogurt churned and frozen — lighter than ice cream, and usually sweeter than it tastes.

tcm.note: Frozen dairy is cold.

ayurveda.note: Dahi is ushna classically, however cold the cup.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Dulce de leche
description: Condensed milk cooked until the sugars caramelise into a thick brown paste.

tcm.note: Read with condensed milk; long cooking warms further.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Custard
description: Milk thickened with egg yolk or powder — poured hot, or set cold.

tcm.note: Milk and egg together.

ayurveda.note: Anda is ushna over a shita milk base.

histamine.note: Egg is a liberator; the powdered versions are mostly cornflour and colour.

name: Cheese powder
description: Dehydrated cheese used to coat crisps and instant pasta.

tcm.note: Inherits from the aged cheese base.

ayurveda.note: Ushna by inheritance.

histamine.note: Built from ripened cheese and stored dry for months.

name: Queso fresco
description: Crumbly fresh white cheese that softens but does not melt.

tcm.note: Fresh unripened cheese.

ayurveda.note: Shita, like paneer.

histamine.note: Fresh and unripened, so low.

name: Cotija
description: Hard salty aged cheese crumbled over corn and beans — the Mexican parmesan.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with the aged cheeses.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Aged cheese.

name: Crema
description: Thinner and less sour than sour cream — poured rather than spooned.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with cultured cream.

ayurveda.note: Soured dairy is ushna.

histamine.note: Cultured but young.

name: Kashk
description: Drained yogurt dried into hard balls and reconstituted — intensely sour and savoury.

tcm.note: Read with yogurt.

ayurveda.note: Soured dairy is ushna.

histamine.note: Yogurt fermented, dried and stored for months — far above fresh dairy.

name: Smen
description: Salted butter buried and aged for months to years — pungent, and used sparingly.

tcm.note: Aged clarified butter.

ayurveda.note: Ghrita is cooling classically, but ageing turns it.

histamine.note: Aged for months to years — the ageing is the whole point.

name: Tvorog
description: Fresh curd cheese, drier than quark — eaten with sour cream or baked into syrniki.

tcm.note: Fresh dairy.

ayurveda.note: Shita; fresh and unsoured.

histamine.note: Fresh and lightly cultured.

name: Ryazhenka
description: Milk baked for hours until caramel-coloured, then cultured — nuttier than kefir.

tcm.note: Long-baked then cultured milk.

ayurveda.note: Baking and souring are both ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam-tar by the baking and ferment.

histamine.note: Cultured dairy; the long bake concentrates it before the ferment even starts.

name: Sguschenka
description: Condensed milk boiled in the tin until it caramelises — eaten with a spoon.

tcm.note: Reduced sweetened milk.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Brynza
description: Sharp white sheep's cheese kept in brine — the Carpathian feta.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; brined cheese; read with feta.

ayurveda.note: Salty and soured, so ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam-khushk by the brine.

histamine.note: Brine-ripened, like feta.

name: Kashkaval
description: Firm yellow sheep or cow cheese, aged and good for grilling.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; read with the aged cheeses.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; ushna and guru.

histamine.note: Aged cheese.

name: Twaróg
description: Polish fresh curd cheese, from soft to dry depending on how long it drains.

tcm.note: Fresh dairy.

ayurveda.note: Shita.

histamine.note: Fresh and unripened.

nutrition.highlight: soft or dry, by draining time

name: Chhena
description: Milk split with acid and drained but not pressed — softer than paneer, and the base of Bengali sweets.

tcm.note: Fresh unpressed curd.

ayurveda.note: Shita and madhura.

histamine.note: Fresh curd, made and used the same day.

name: Shanklish
description: Cheese balls rolled in za'atar and aged until sharp, sometimes until they crumble.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; an aged and mould-ripened cheese.

ayurveda.note: Aged and ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam-khushk by ageing.

histamine.note: Deliberately aged and often mould-ripened — as high as cheese gets.

name: Jameed
description: Sheep yogurt salted, drained and sun-dried into hard stones, reconstituted for mansaf.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; dried fermented dairy.

ayurveda.note: Soured, so ushna.

histamine.note: A fermented yogurt dried hard — the ferment concentrates as the water goes.

nutrition.highlight: hard as a stone, and meant to be

name: Jibneh baladi
description: Plain fresh white cheese kept in brine — mild, squeaky, and eaten at every breakfast.

tcm.note: Fresh brined cheese.

ayurveda.note: Shita and madhura.

histamine.note: Brined rather than aged, so lower than the ripened cheeses.

name: Skyr
description: A thick strained cultured skimmed milk — technically a cheese, eaten as yogurt.

tcm.note: Cultured strained dairy.

ayurveda.note: Shita.

histamine.note: Cultured, though the cultures used are milder than yogurt's.

nutrition.highlight: technically a cheese, eaten as yogurt
